links.outcome: Standalone GPT-4 versus human reviewer detection of adverse events, not human-AI team performance
links.effect: GPT-4 sensitivity 100.0% vs 89.8% for humans for durotomy, but PPV 88.0% vs 100.0%; GPT-4 was not evaluated with humans in the loop.
links.quote: GPT-4 achieved 100.0% sensitivity compared with 89.8% for human reviewers, with lower positive predictive value (88.0% vs 100.0%) but similar specificity (99.1% vs 100.0%).

links.outcome: GPT-4 compared with trained human reviewers on same notes, sensitivity and specificity
links.effect: For nondurotomy adverse events (n=21), GPT-4 sensitivity 90.5% vs 57.1% for humans, with equivalent 100.0% specificity.
links.quote: For nondurotomy adverse events (n = 21), GPT-4 demonstrated higher sensitivity than humans (90.5% vs 57.1%) with equivalent specificity (100.0%).

links.outcome: Performance stability across operative note length quartiles
links.effect: GPT-4 maintained stable performance across note length quartiles, whereas human reviewer sensitivity decreased for longer notes.
links.quote: GPT-4 maintained stable performance across note length quartiles, whereas human reviewer sensitivity decreased for longer notes.

unlisted_practices: LLM-assisted chart review for research data abstraction with human-in-the-loop adjudication

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation comparing GPT-4 against human chart review for identifying adverse events in operative notes without evaluating a specific deployment safeguard or operational intervention.
